27 That they should seek the Lord, if haply they might feel after him, and find him, though he be not far from every one of us: (Acts 17:27 KJV)

We all need to seek the Lord, and the statement “feel after him” is like a blind man feeling his way, not knowing where he is going, but just groping around after Him. The truth is that God is not far from all of us, and if we seek after Him with all our hearts, we will find Him (Jeremiah 29:13). Saying that we find God is not really correct, as God is not the one that was lost, but we were. God wants us to fellowship with Him, and will answer us when we search for Him with all our hearts (Matthew 5:6). Finding God is just the first step, as getting to know God in a intimate way, is what we need to do. Being born again is absolutely necessary, but getting to know God through the study of His Word (Romans 12:2), is what brings us the eternal life (John 3:16) that makes the Christian life so awesome. After being born again we must then obey Jesus to assure our eternal salvation (Hebrews 5:9). Knowing God’s love, and the peace it brings, makes a real difference in our lives.

Once we have found God, or He has found us, and we have been born again, then God lives in us from then on, and we become one with Him (John 17:11). That is such a wonderful thing, and has been a fact that we have a hard time comprehending, as we are in Him, and He is in us, and we have become one with Him. That is beyond our capacity to fully understand, as it is in the spiritual realm, and us carnal humans have a hard time understanding that. What we have to do is know that God’s Word is true, and accept what it is telling us about spiritual things, as the Word of God is Spirit and Truth (John 17:17). Thank you Lord for your Word!

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com

IPFS, one of the developing technologies of the decentalized global network.

It sounds interesting and I'll be giving it a try.

I do have one initial bit of scepticism with all P2P networks, in hardware terms most devices are not peers. I don't want my tablet to participate in a Skype type network, nor having to host massive amounts of copies for distribution, even though I am happy for my servers to do the same.

I have a lot a skeptism about P2P networks in general for two reasons:

  1. They don't change the physical topology of a network so they are really more pseudo P2P because all of the hops required to get somewhere else on the network don't change. The result is that if I need to read a file stored on someone's computer on the other side of the world it's going to suck because they probably have a asymmetrical links provided by their ISP who probably also completely disallows serving of any sort. That can't ever be better than connecting to a dedicated data center designed to handle large amounts of traffic from the start with fast compute and storage doing the serving.

  2. The mesh network idea disregards the realities of routing and switching times. I want as few hops between me and the other computer as possible and it's not at all clear how such networks would provide for long haul communication over sparsely populated areas. Moving things quickly requires bandwidth which requires very high frequencies but they don't carry very far and HF has shit for bandwidth and can't carry data very fast. Throw in speed of light and switching/routing delays and it just doesn't work.
So do your points boil down in to the simple fact that not enough people use it? No agenda here, just curious.

No I'm saying it doesn't matter how many people use it because either the underlying network doesn't change (your ISP) or you have a problem with long haul and determining the best path to the peer you're trying to reach.

I could be missing something but I can't imagine how it could possibly change the way we access the internet.
I don't think you are missing anything. Also, thank you for the clarification. As much of a fan of mesh/distributed networks that I am, this alone makes me very sad for the outlook on their future.
